I found the problem: I should have used this version of the pdf.

the actual command is: INLA:::inla.display.matrix()

What it actually means I have no idea, but it works!

On Thu, 2014-11-20 at 10:25 -0800, Christoph Konrad wrote:
>
> I found the problem: I should have used this version of the pdf.
>
> the actual command is: INLA:::inla.display.matrix()
>
> What it actually means I have no idea, but it works!

sorry about that. from R-3.0 all libraries must declare function to be
exported, ie visible from outside the package. exported functions needs
to be properly documented, and only those 'needed' should be that. this
is an internal helper function, which simply display a matrix in matrix
way, with element [1,1] in the top left corner.

to access an internal function fun in library LIB, call LIB:::fun(),
hence the format above

H
